title: 2WIE 2026 Talk
text:
Contents

Abstract
Interceptions reveal locations and sequences, but not every actor or connection. The talk frames the problem as inference on the unobserved vertices and edges of a spatio-temporal criminal network, and proposes a reproducible build–reconstruct–validate pipeline:

Chronnet construction — 586 HF communications from 2018 → 333 vertices and 1,105 directed edges, with accounting identities for verification.
Supervised reconstruction — classification under extreme imbalance (≈ 1 % edges): PCA + SMOTE + logistic regression, selected by specificity (47 false positives vs. 334 and 1,339).
Unobserved elements — 107 candidate unknown edges and 84 unique hidden vertices, with spatial validation (Wilcoxon tests by infrastructure and scale) and operational validation with CENAC-DIJIN and DIRAN.

Authors: Andrés Pérez-Coronado · Gustavo Canavire-Bacarreza · Santiago Ortíz · Henry Laniado (FastAnalytics S.A.S)
Scientific talk — 2nd International Meeting on Statistics 2026, Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Manizales Campus · November 5–6, 2026 · La Nubia Campus, R and W blocks.

The presentation is organized in three parts:







Part
Contents




Problem and data
Observable subnetwork, element typology (known, unknown, hidden), 586 HF records from 2018


Method
Chronnet construction (equations 1–3), dyadic dataset, SMOTE and model selection, hidden-vertex search with homophily


Results and decision
In-sample reconstruction (97 % of edges), unknown edges (107) and hidden vertices (84), spatial proximity rule, policy implications
